links.outcome: Recognition of high-acuity patients (safety-critical situations) by LLMs versus triage nurses
links.effect: ChatGPT and Copilot recognized high-acuity patients better than nurses (87.8% and 85.7% versus 32.7%); nurses significantly under-triaged patients (p < 0.05).
links.quote: In recognizing high-acuity patients, ChatGPT and Copilot outperformed triage nurses (87.8 % and 85.7 % versus 32.7 %, respectively).

links.outcome: Triage accuracy of LLMs compared with triage nurses against EM physician reference
links.effect: Overall accuracy 65.2% nurses, 66.5% ChatGPT, 61.8% Copilot; Cohen's Kappa 0.537 ChatGPT, 0.477 nurses, 0.472 Copilot.
links.quote: The overall triage accuracy was 65.2 % for nurses, 66.5 % for ChatGPT, and 61.8 % for Copilot, with no significant difference (p = 0.000).

screen.reason: The study evaluates the triage performance of ChatGPT Plus and Copilot Pro against triage nurses on clinical vignettes documented by an EM physician, but does not test a specific deployment safeguard or practice.
